TS-Pico 2.3.1 is firmware 2.3.1 with the unchanged ROM 2.3. It's the first release for the **TS-Pico v3 card** (RP2350B), as well as the TS-Pico 2.x boards. On a 2.x board running 2.3, nothing changes in use.

**Coming from 1.1?** Read [What's new in the TS-Pico since 1.1](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/updates/whats-new-since-1-1/).

## The v3 card

The same firmware runs on the v3 card, with the same commands, LOAD and SAVE, `tpi:` commands, printer and ZX Spectrum mode. The user manual's **Appendix F** covers what's different:

- **ROMs and cartridges live in slot files** on the card (`/slots`), not a flash chip. `tpi:boot` and `tpi:dock` switch slots as on 2.x. A slot pair in RAM gives a program **64K of RAM in the dock**.
- **Writing a ROM or cartridge into a slot** (`LOAD "tpi:file.dck"` and the loader, as in 8.4) is done by the card itself, in a fraction of a second.
- **The SD socket's card-detect switch** is read before the SD lines are touched, so cards can be swapped between commands safely, and "No SD card" comes back at once.
- **Power cycles with the card on USB.** The card holds the 2068 in reset while it's off and briefly after it comes back on, so it boots cleanly every time.

Found and fixed on the way:

- On the v3 card, `LOAD "tpi:file.tap"` in ZX Spectrum mode failed with "1 NEXT without FOR". The cause: while the card writes its own flash, part of the RP2350's bus stalls for microseconds. The card's IN handling no longer goes through that part. (#254)
- On the v3 card, `tpi:dock` answered before the dock had switched, so a program's next PEEK could read an empty dock. (#253)

## For everyone

- **The user manual:** Appendix F (the v3 card); PDFs restyled after the 1983 TS 2068 User Manual; and **start a cartridge with `NEW`** (or TS Reset), not `OUT 244,3`, which is ZX Spectrum mode's switch. (#251, #232, #258)
- **`tools/hwcheck.py`** runs the hardware checklist on either board, mostly unattended. (#253, #256)

## Installing

**A TS-Pico 2.x board:**

1. **Switch the TS-2068 off.**
2. Open the [web updater](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/updater/) in Chrome or Edge, connect the TS-Pico by USB, choose **Latest release**, and follow the steps. On Windows you can run **TS-Pico-Updater.exe** from this release instead.
3. A board already on ROM 2.3 needs only the firmware. The updater ticks **Update the TS-2068 ROM** for a board not on 2.3; leave it ticked then.
4. Keep the **P10 jumper** fitted.

**The v3 card:**

1. Open the [web updater](https://timex-sinclair-projects.github.io/tspico-firmware-build/updater/) in Chrome or Edge, connect the card by USB, choose **Latest release**, and follow the steps. It installs the firmware and the ROM and cartridge slots, and keeps any slots you've filled. The Windows updater doesn't handle the v3 card yet.
2. Or by hand: hold BOOTSEL while plugging in, and drag `firmware-v3.uf2` onto the **RP2350** drive. A card being set up for the first time also needs its ROM slots. The web updater puts them in place; `v3-slots.zip` holds the same files, for copying into `/slots` on the card with Thonny or `mpremote` (the card's flash isn't a USB drive).

Afterwards, `SAVE "tpi:info"` shows firmware 2.3.1 and ROM 2.3. `PRINT PEEK 101` gives **35** (ROM 2.3).

## Downloads

- `firmware.uf2`: the TS-Pico 2.x firmware, for dragging onto the Pico's RPI-RP2 drive by hand.
- `firmware-v3.uf2`: the v3 card's firmware, for its RP2350 drive.
- `v3-slots.zip`: the v3 card's ROM and cartridge slot files, for `/slots`.
- `upgrade.uf2`: the ROM updater (2.x boards).
- `TS-Pico-Updater.exe`: the updater for Windows (2.x boards).
- `Pico-v2.3.1.rom`: the whole 512K flash image (2.x boards).
- `user-manual-half-letter.pdf`, `user-manual-saddle-stitch-letter.pdf`: the user manual.
- `pico_host-*.zip`: the TS-Pico firmware for emulators, for macOS, Linux and Windows. Use it with ROM 2.3. See the emulator guide.
- The release zip: the firmware, the Pico's files, ROM 2.3 (`src/rom/TSPICO-23.ROM`) and the SD card files.
